query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: ticket_category
per_column.rationale: A strong grouping axis for resolution time; category types (bug, outage, feature) plausibly correlate with resolution duration. Values are well-grounded in the issue text across samples.

per_column.name: product_area
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis for comparing resolution time by affected component. Values map cleanly to described modules (billing, SSO, export pipeline), with reasonable NULLs for silent rows.

per_column.name: reported_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity is a plausible driver of resolution time and adds leverage beyond the existing priority column. Mostly grounded; the billing duplicate line item as 'degraded_non_blocking' is a defensible reading, though such gradations involve some interpretation.

per_column.name: business_deadline_pressure
per_column.rationale: Deadline pressure is a meaningful signal that could influence handling speed. Values track the text (Friday books close = hard_deadline; renewal parity = soft_urgency). The outage 'immediate' rated soft rather than hard is arguable but not a clear error.

per_column.name: affected_user_scope
per_column.rationale: Blast radius is a strong predictor of resolution effort. Values are well-grounded (single user vs entire tenant 502). Export affecting the tenant is a reasonable inference.

per_column.name: environment_scope
per_column.rationale: Prod vs non-prod can correlate with urgency and complexity, giving analytical value. Heavily 'not_specified' (178) which limits leverage, but grounded values are sound and silent rows correctly marked.

per_column.name: root_cause_type
per_column.rationale: Root cause is highly relevant to resolution difficulty. However, the billing duplicate-line-item ticket is labeled 'regression_code_bug' with no textual support for a code regression, an unwarranted specific. Other samples are reasonable, but this contradicts the silent source.

per_column.name: regression_after_change
per_column.rationale: A regression flag is a plausible resolution-time signal but partially redundant with root_cause_type/ticket_category. Values grounded: '4.7 release' -> true, SSO push suspicion left false is conservative and acceptable.

per_column.name: reproducibility
per_column.rationale: Reproducibility genuinely affects diagnosis time. Values largely sound (session drops every 12-15 min as intermittent is defensible). Marking the billing invoice as 'consistently_reproducible' is a mild stretch but not a clear error.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide multiple genuinely distinct axes (category, product area, severity, deadline pressure, blast radius, root cause, regression, reproducibility) that all plausibly relate to why a ticket takes longer to resolve, giving strong analytical leverage with little redundancy. Groundedness is generally high and silent rows are appropriately marked 'not_present'/'not_specified'. The main weakness is occasional over-confident inference, most notably root_cause_type='regression_code_bug' for the billing ticket that offers no evidence of a code regression, plus mild severity/reproducibility stretches.
